units.passage: Do not use AI to create or distribute malicious content, including malware, viruses, phishing emails, or any other content designed to harm individuals, systems, or networks. Such uses are prohibited under University Policy Number 1301 on the responsible use of computing. Intellectual Property Infringement: Do not use AI to create or distribute content that violates copyright or intellectual property laws per University Policy Number 1104 on copyrighted materials. Be aware that the use of AI-generated images in official university materials and any AI-generated materials produced using university resources currently bear high intellectual property risks and could expose the university to liability. Deception and Misinformation: Do not use AI to deceive others. This includes creating false communication, such as fake news articles, fabricated messages, or misleading information, with the intent to deceive or manipulate others. Do not use AI to alter or fabricate data to support false claims or mislead
units.why: 'Do not use AI to alter or fabricate data to support false claims or mislead' is a general-conduct ban on deceptive AI use; it is not specific to research (P62) or to coursework, so no type fits and it is UNCOVERED like the neighbouring deception bans.
units.uncovered_note: General-conduct ban on using AI to fabricate or alter data or to deceive; not a teaching or learning rule and no type covers it.

units.passage: Unauthorized Surveillance: Do not use AI for any form of unauthorized surveillance of individuals on university grounds or within university systems.
units.why: 'Do not use AI for any form of unauthorized surveillance of individuals' is a surveillance prohibition with no fitting type.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI for unauthorized surveillance of students, faculty or staff.

units.passage: Harassment and Abuse: Do not use AI to harass, bully, or intimidate.
units.why: 'Do not use AI to harass, bully, or intimidate' is a conduct prohibition; no type, UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to harass, bully, intimidate or generate hate speech.

units.passage: Set yourself apart by personalizing and customizing your materials.
units.why: On-campus employers report AI-generated cover letters that 'begin to sound the same', so the page advises 'Set yourself apart by personalizing and customizing your materials'; this is non-course job-application advice and fits no type.
units.uncovered_note: Advice on job applications: personalize AI-assisted cover letters so they do not sound alike. Not coursework.

units.passage: The use of AI to create or spread false or misleading information about courses or instructors violates university policies
units.why: 'use of AI to create or spread false or misleading information about courses or instructors violates university policies'; harmful-content prohibition with no fitting type.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to create or spread false information about courses or instructors (non-coursework misconduct).

units.passage: If the review committee suspects or can tell that you have used AI, your application will be rejected.
units.why: 'If the review committee suspects or can tell that you have used AI, your application will be rejected' is a scholarship-application warning, uncovered.
units.uncovered_note: Advice about AI use in job, on-campus employment and scholarship applications (not coursework).

units.passage: Don't use AI to impersonate instructors or other students, in ways that disrupt classes or threaten instructors or fellow students
units.why: 'Don't use AI to impersonate instructors or other students'; harmful-conduct prohibition, no fitting type.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to impersonate, disrupt or threaten instructors and students.

units.passage: Don't use AI to generate false or misleading academic records or recommendations
units.why: 'Don't use AI to generate false or misleading academic records or recommendations'; fabrication ban, no fitting type.
units.uncovered_note: General-conduct ban on using AI to fabricate academic records or recommendations.

units.passage: We recommend not using language that suggests that AI tools “compose” or “write” texts; they are algorithms assembling words and producing text using a prescribed data set.
units.why: 'We recommend not using language that suggests that AI tools "compose" or "write" texts' is advice on wording; no codebook type.
units.uncovered_note: Advice on how instructors should word or talk about AI (avoid anthropomorphic language).

units.passage: Require at all levels meticulous citing of peer-reviewed and published work and identify the reason for this.
units.why: "Require at all levels meticulous citing of peer-reviewed and published work and identify the reason for this" tells instructors to require citation of sources in general and states no link to AI; no listed type states that (P24 and P25 are about citing AI use), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors require meticulous citation of peer-reviewed and published sources generally (not AI-specific disclosure).

units.passage: Your human skills as instructors continue to be your best defense against dishonesty, and education about why integrity is important to the communication of knowledge is key.
units.why: "education about why integrity is important ... is key" and instructors’ human skills are the best defense; integrity education, not tooling. No type fits (P41, P57 not about this), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Teaching why integrity matters, rather than detection, is the main defense against AI-enabled dishonesty.

units.passage: Members of the Georgetown community should take steps to maintain the security and integrity of Georgetown resources.
units.why: "should take steps to maintain the security and integrity of Georgetown resources" is a security duty. No type covers security of institutional systems (P50 is personal data and vetted tools), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Maintain the security and integrity of university resources when using AI

units.passage: If you suspect an assignment has been completed dishonestly, we advise to follow a mosaic approach
units.why: "we advise to follow a mosaic approach" to suspected dishonest AI use names a method whose content is not given on this page; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Follow a 'mosaic approach' when suspecting AI-completed work (method described on a linked page)

units.passage: It is, as always, the students’ responsibility to be sure that they are following the rules laid out by their professors.
units.why: "It is, as always, the students' responsibility to be sure that they are following the rules laid out by their professors" puts the duty of knowing course rules on students. P10 (ask when unsure) and P29 (own submissions) do not say this, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Students are responsible for knowing and following the AI rules their professors set

units.passage: Involving your students in the AI policy writing process is a great way not only to get them to reflect on their own learning habits, but also to learn about their AI usage and get their buy-in for class ground rules.
units.why: "Involving your students in the AI policy writing process is a great way..." recommends co-creating course AI policy with students. No type covers co-creation (P04 is who decides; P09 is stating the policy), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Co-create the course AI policy with students to gain reflection and buy-in

units.passage: Of course, requiring a declaration from students may also increase your own workload, as it provides you with another detail to attend to as you grade. Taking stock of this tradeoff is an important calculus as you develop your policy.
units.why: "requiring a declaration from students may also increase your own workload ... Taking stock of this tradeoff is an important calculus" warns instructors about grading burden, which no type names, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should weigh the extra grading workload of required AI declarations against their benefits. / Instructors should weigh the extra grading workload against the benefit of requiring AI declarations.

units.passage: Training on risks, compliance, and acceptable and ethical use of AI is a component of the required yearly training for all faculty, staff, and students.
units.why: "Training on risks, compliance, and acceptable and ethical use of AI is a component of the required yearly training for all faculty, staff, and students" mandates training for everyone. P63 covers voluntary support for faculty learning AI, not required training for the whole community, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.passage: Compliance Recordkeeping: Keep internal records of AI approvals, audits, and compliance activities to ensure accountability and support regulatory reporting obligations. The Office of Institutional Research and Effectiveness will maintain records of compliance and documentation Page 3 of 9 for audit or investigation purposes.
units.why: "Keep internal records of AI approvals, audits, and compliance activities", with Institutional Research maintaining the records, is an imperative administrative duty. P54 is about revisiting the policy, and no type covers compliance recordkeeping, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Institutional recordkeeping of AI approvals, audits and compliance activities.

units.passage: Complete the required AI training provided by the University.
units.why: Students must "Complete the required AI training provided by the University". P63 supports faculty learning AI; mandatory student training fits no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.passage: Staff must complete training in the ethical use of AI in the workplace, and as appropriate to their responsibilities.
units.why: "Staff must complete training in the ethical use of AI in the workplace" is a mandatory training duty, which P63 (support for faculty) does not cover, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.passage: The University requires training to ensure faculty, staff, and students are well-equipped to engage with AI in a responsible, ethical, and informed manner.
units.why: "The University requires training to ensure faculty, staff, and students are well-equipped to engage with AI" is a training mandate for all members, which no type covers, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.passage: Students will have access to additional educational programs designed to build their understanding of AI tools, promote responsible usage, and highlight potential risks.
units.why: "Students will have access to additional educational programs designed to build their understanding of AI tools, promote responsible usage, and highlight potential risks" offers AI education to students. P63 is about supporting faculty, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: University-provided AI education programs for students (not faculty support).

units.passage: Supervision - It is the responsibility of the supervising faculty member to ensure that their students and post-doctoral fellows complete the required training and are aware of and comply with this policy.
units.why: "It is the responsibility of the supervising faculty member to ensure that their students and post-doctoral fellows complete the required training" is a duty to see that mandatory training is done. It is not support for faculty learning AI (P63), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Required AI training for faculty, staff and students (compliance training, not faculty-support workshops).

units.passage: Any discrepancies or issues must be reported to IIT and addressed promptly.
units.why: "must be reported to IIT and addressed promptly" is an incident-reporting duty for AI tool problems. It is not data protection (P50) or output verification (P31) itself, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Duty to report AI tool discrepancies or issues to IIT

units.passage: Consider co-creating AI usage guidelines with your students .
units.why: "Consider co-creating AI usage guidelines with your students" proposes a participatory way of setting the rule; P04 sets rules per instructor but not co-creation, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Co-create AI usage guidelines with students

units.passage: Consider co-creating AI usage guidelines with your students .
units.why: "Consider co-creating AI usage guidelines with your students" proposes a participatory way of setting the rule; P04 sets rules per instructor but not co-creation, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Co-create AI usage guidelines with students

units.passage: AI tools should be monitored and validated to ensure they produce results as intended, and any discrepancies or issues should be reported promptly to the University AI Committee at [email protected] or to IIT at
units.policy: Any discrepancies or issues with AI tools should be reported promptly to the University AI Committee or to IIT.
units.why: Issues 'should be reported promptly to the University AI Committee': tool-issue reporting, no type fits.
units.uncovered_note: Duty to report AI tool discrepancies or issues

units.passage: It remains crucial to adhere to security best practices and to report any dubious messages to phishing@gatech.edu
units.why: "adhere to security best practices and to report any dubious messages" is a security reporting duty about AI-enabled phishing; no type covers phishing vigilance, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Be vigilant about AI-enabled phishing and deepfakes and report suspicious messages to the security address.

units.passage: Once the concern is reported, the instructor should not discuss the case with the student except under guidance from the AIO. The instructor will continue to teach and engage with the student as they would any other learner in the class
units.why: "the instructor should not discuss the case with the student except under guidance from the AIO" bars instructors from confronting students. This is the opposite of P57 (talk before escalating), so UNCOVERED: no type covers a rule that instructors must not discuss a suspected violation with the student.
units.uncovered_note: Rule that instructors must not discuss a suspected violation with the student except under AIO guidance (opposite of P57).

units.passage: You do not need to make an iron-clad case or do extensive investigation, but you should provide sufficient information for the committee to understand your concern
units.why: "You do not need to make an iron-clad case or do extensive investigation" sets the evidence bar for referral. P40 is about which methods are used to identify misuse; this is a threshold for reporting, which no type covers.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors need not build an iron-clad case or investigate extensively before referring a suspected violation; sufficient information for the committee to understand the concern is enough.

units.passage: Stating that the work “doesn’t sound like [student]” or “doesn’t sound like a college student” is not sufficient evidence
units.why: Saying the work "doesn't sound like [student]" is "not sufficient evidence", ruling out impressionistic judgment as proof. P39 does not fit (not about detectors) and P40 lists methods rather than excluding one, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Evidence standard: impressionistic claims that work does not sound like the student are not sufficient evidence of misuse.

units.passage: You should not engage with the student regarding the potential violation. You should notify the student that you have submitted their work to CAS and they will be contacted about next steps, but you should not ask them for an explanation or discuss further your concerns
units.why: "You should not engage with the student regarding the potential violation ... you should not ask them for an explanation" tells faculty not to confront the student. This conflicts with P57, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Faculty must not question or discuss concerns with the student after referring a suspected violation.

units.passage: AAI may be used to increase student service operations that support advising, retention, and graduation.
units.why: "AAI may be used to increase student service operations that support advising, retention, and graduation" permits agentic AI for student services; it is administrative use, not teaching, and no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Permits agentic AI for administrative student-service operations (advising, retention, graduation); not teaching or learning use.

units.passage: These agents may be used to enhance operational workflows, communications, data analysis, and service delivery, provided outputs are reviewed for accuracy and appropriateness.
units.why: "These agents may be used to enhance operational workflows, communications, data analysis, and service delivery, provided outputs are reviewed" permits administrative AI use with review; no type for administrative operations, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Permits agentic AI for operational workflows, communications and data analysis with output review; administrative use.

units.passage: AI-generated outputs used in official University operations, communications, or decision-support must be reviewed by a human prior to use
units.why: 'AI-generated outputs used in official University operations ... must be reviewed by a human prior to use' requires staff review of operational output; no type covers administrative operations, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Human review required before AI outputs are used in official university operations, communications or decision support.

units.passage: AI may not be used to make final decisions regarding employment, finances, academic standing, or disciplinary actions without appropriate human oversight
units.why: 'AI may not be used to make final decisions regarding employment, finances, academic standing, or disciplinary actions without appropriate human oversight' limits AI in institutional decisions beyond grades (P46), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: No AI final decisions on employment, finances, academic standing or discipline without human oversight; broader than grading (P46).

units.passage: The Division of Information Technology may restrict access to AI tools that pose institutional risk.
units.why: 'The Division of Information Technology may restrict access to AI tools that pose institutional risk' lets IT block tools; P50 does not cover institutional blocking, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: IT division may restrict access to AI tools posing institutional risk.

units.passage: In instances when collaborative work is assigned, we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated.
units.why: 'we expect for the assignment to list all team members who participated' requires students to name contributors on collaborative work. It sits inside the AI sample policy but is about attributing human collaborators, not AI use, and no type covers it.
units.uncovered_note: Collaborative assignments must list all team members who participated (attribution of human contributors, not AI use).

units.passage: While there are technologies for exam proctoring that aim to block students from using the internet, FAS does not plan to provide/license such a tool for use in courses.
units.policy: FAS does not plan to provide or license an exam-proctoring tool that blocks students from using the internet in courses.
units.why: 'FAS does not plan to provide/license' an internet-blocking exam-proctoring tool; it is a statement about what the institution will not supply for exams, which fits no type (P22 bans AI on exams; P33 shifts to proctored assessment).
units.uncovered_note: FAS does not plan to provide or license an internet-blocking exam-proctoring tool for courses.

units.passage: All students in this course are expected to adhere to this course policy around generative AI tools.
units.policy: All students in this course are expected to adhere to this course policy around generative AI tools.
units.why: "All students in this course are expected to adhere to this course policy around generative AI tools" binds students to follow the course policy; P29 (own what you submit) does not fit, so UNCOVERED, student, during-work, must.
units.uncovered_note: Students must adhere to the course's own AI policy.

units.passage: While we recognize that these technologies are advancing very quickly, it is helpful to tell students what tools/resources are reliable sources of information to give them alternatives to unreliable tools.
units.policy: It is helpful for instructors to tell students what tools and resources are reliable sources of information, to give alternatives to unreliable tools.
units.why: Advises instructors to point students to reliable alternatives to unreliable AI tools. P31 is addressed to students verifying output, so this instructor practice fits no type and is UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors recommend reliable sources and alternatives to students as a way to reduce reliance on unreliable AI tools.

units.passage: performing a calculation (e.g. an ugly integral) that you already know how to perform (note: there are more reliable tools for mathematical calculations than gen AI);
units.why: Level 1 allows AI to do a calculation the student already knows how to do. No type covers calculation help, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Allowing AI to perform routine calculations the student already knows how to do (time-saving use).

units.passage: performing a calculation or ancillary task, but not one that is novel and central to your idea;
units.why: Level 2 allows AI for calculation or ancillary tasks that are not central. No type covers calculation help, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Allowing AI to perform calculations or ancillary tasks that are not novel and central to the student's idea.

units.passage: Agents must use unique, non-human identities (service accounts) with dedicated credentials
units.why: "Agents must use unique, non-human identities (service accounts) with dedicated credentials" is a technical access-control rule for deployed agents; no type covers it (P07 is about student use of agents in coding work), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Security rules for identity and credentials of AI agents that people develop or deploy.

units.passage: Enforce least privilege across systems, data, and tools Grant access only to required skills and resources Default tool access to read-only unless explicitly required otherwise
units.policy: Enforce least privilege across systems, data, and tools; grant access only to required skills and resources; default tool access to read-only unless explicitly required otherwise.
units.why: "Enforce least privilege across systems, data, and tools", with "Grant access only to required skills and resources" and read-only default tool access, is an access-control rule for AI agents; no type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Least-privilege and read-only access control for AI agents.

units.passage: Clearly define the agent’s purpose and allowed operations Restrict agents to operate only within their intended scope Prevent execution of actions outside defined intent Apply graduated autonomy based on risk level Require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions
units.policy: Define each agent's purpose and allowed operations, restrict it to its intended scope, apply graduated autonomy based on risk level, and require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions.
units.why: "Require human-in-the-loop approval for high-risk actions" with "graduated autonomy based on risk" and defined agent scope limits what agents may do. It is not about decisions on people (P73), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Limits on the scope and autonomy of deployed AI agents, with human approval for high-risk actions.

units.passage: Control and govern communication between agents Prevent unintended privilege escalation through agent chaining Ensure combined agent workflows do not exceed intended authority Carefully design deployment architecture to enforce separation of duties
units.policy: Control and govern communication between agents, prevent unintended privilege escalation through agent chaining, ensure combined workflows do not exceed intended authority, and design deployment architecture to enforce separation of duties.
units.why: "Control and govern communication between agents" and prevent "privilege escalation through agent chaining" are architecture controls for multi-agent systems; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Architecture controls for multi-agent AI systems (communication, privilege escalation, separation of duties).

units.passage: If reusing the model for a different purpose, reset it back to the foundational model as residual training data may remain and may lead to unintended consequences
units.policy: If reusing a hosted model for a different purpose, reset it back to the foundational model, as residual training data may remain and may lead to unintended consequences.
units.why: "If reusing the model for a different purpose, reset it back to the foundational model as residual training data may remain" is a hosting hygiene rule fitting no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Advice to reset a self-hosted model to its foundational state before reuse to avoid leaking residual training data.

units.passage: Continue to follow security best practices and report suspicious messages to huhelpdesk@howard.edu
units.why: Tells users to 'report suspicious messages to huhelpdesk@howard.edu' about AI-enabled phishing; a security rule outside the closed list, UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Report suspicious messages: the guidance asks everyone to be alert for AI-enabled phishing and report suspicious messages to the help desk. This is cybersecurity guidance, not protection of personal data.

units.passage: AI text generators can create annotated bibliographies that give insights into potential primary and secondary source material.
units.why: "Collect Sources" with "annotated bibliographies" is a permitted use for finding source material, which no existing type names.
units.uncovered_note: AI used to find and annotate primary and secondary sources for research (generating annotated bibliographies).

units.passage: We recommend faculty adopt a proactive rather than punitive approach to the use of AI .
units.why: "We recommend faculty adopt a proactive rather than punitive approach to the use of AI" gives a stance on handling AI that fits no listed type (P57 is about talking before escalating, P35 about redesign).
units.uncovered_note: Faculty should take a proactive rather than punitive approach to student AI use.

units.passage: Students who understand the purpose of their assignments and are invested in their own learning are less likely to over rely on AI tools.
units.policy: Students who understand the purpose of their assignments and are invested in their own learning are less likely to over rely on AI tools.
units.why: 'Students who understand the purpose of their assignments and are invested in their own learning are less likely to over rely on AI tools' ties over-reliance to students' grasp of assignment purpose. No type covers it: P41 is about AI shortcutting skill practice, which the passage does not say.
units.uncovered_note: Explaining assignment purposes and building student investment reduces over-reliance on AI.

units.passage: It is not recommended to simply replace existing high-stakes assignments with graded, hand-written, in-class assignments. This may have unintended consequences for students who use technology to provide accommodations and other legitimate assistance in completing coursework.
units.why: "It is not recommended to simply replace existing high-stakes assignments with graded, hand-written, in-class assignments" warns against moving to in-class work because it harms students with accommodations: P33 in reverse.
units.uncovered_note: Advises against simply replacing existing high-stakes assignments with graded, hand-written, in-class assignments, because this may have unintended consequences for students who use technology for accommodations and other legitimate assistance.

units.passage: When evaluating concerns, faculty should focus on course expectations, assignment requirements, the student's work product, and any other relevant information rather than relying on AI-detection tools alone.
units.why: "faculty should focus on course expectations, assignment requirements, the student's work product, and any other relevant information" says what evidence instructors weigh when judging a suspected AI concern. P40 covers detection tools and process logs and P57 covers talking with the student; neither covers weighing course expectations and work product, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Prescribes which evidence faculty should weigh (course expectations, assignment requirements, work product, other information) when judging suspected AI misuse.

units.passage: In accordance with EO 46, JMU faculty, staff, employees, affiliates, and contractors are prohibited from using DeepSeek AI Chatbot, or other tools developed by DeepSeek, on any Commonwealth of Virginia issued devices or through Commonwealth of Virginia owned, operated, or maintained wireless networks.
units.why: 'are prohibited from using DeepSeek AI Chatbot, or other tools developed by DeepSeek' on Commonwealth devices and networks is a rule that bans a named tool for faculty, staff, affiliates and contractors. It is a general rule (not tied to a course phase), must-not, and fits no type: P50 is about protecting data and preferring vetted tools, not banning one product.
units.uncovered_note: A ban on one named AI tool (DeepSeek) on Commonwealth devices and networks, imposed by state Executive Order 46. No existing type covers a named-tool ban.

units.passage: Remind students of academic integrity obligations , including the practical consequences of academic integrity violations
units.policy: Instructors remind students of academic integrity obligations, including the practical consequences of academic integrity violations.
units.why: 'Remind students of academic integrity obligations, including the practical consequences of academic integrity violations' tells instructors to communicate integrity duties and consequences; no type covers reminding students of consequences specifically (P36 classifies misuse, P37 states penalties), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors remind students of their academic integrity obligations and the consequences of violations. (Coder B's fit note, from a P36 assignment: it is a reminder duty for instructors; it does not say that unauthorized AI use is misconduct.)

units.passage: We are also planning workshops and discussions to help faculty to learn to use AI effectively, and we will encourage department and school conversations about applying consistent approaches to the use of AI.
units.policy: we will encourage department and school conversations about applying consistent approaches to the use of AI
units.why: 'we will encourage department and school conversations about applying consistent approaches to the use of AI' promotes shared approaches at unit level; none of the types fit (P85 lets units set their own rules), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: CTE will encourage departments and schools to talk about applying consistent approaches to AI use. | CTE encourages department and school conversations to reach consistent approaches to AI use.

units.passage: If you choose to use GAI to assist you in any part of your assignments, you must follow these policies: Be prepared to support your choice of using GAI for your assignments. Indicate and cite any AI-generated or AI-assisted parts of assignments.
units.why: Nursing example: 'Be prepared to support your choice of using GAI for your assignments' asks students to justify their choice; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Students must be prepared to justify their choice to use generative AI in an assignment. | Students must be ready to justify their decision to use generative AI on an assignment.

units.passage: Analyzing generative AI tools and their outputs as part of an assignment is not the same as using them to complete your assignments
units.policy: Analyzing generative AI tools and their outputs as part of an assignment is not the same as using them to complete your assignments.
units.why: English HNRS 190: 'Analyzing generative AI tools and their outputs as part of an assignment is not the same as using them to complete your assignments' separates studying AI from using it; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Analyzing AI tools and outputs as an object of study is distinguished from using AI to complete an assignment.

units.passage: Any guidelines or policy should include approaches to handling misuse of AI. AI detectors are unreliable and do not provide proof of student misconduct.
units.why: Important considerations: 'Any guidelines or policy should include approaches to handling misuse of AI' asks instructors to plan for misuse; no type fits exactly, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors' AI policies should include an approach to handling misuse. | Instructor policies should say how AI misuse will be handled.

units.passage: Users should be aware that the use of Generative AI may create University records that fall under the Kansas Opens Record Act.
units.why: 'Users should be aware that the use of Generative AI may create University records that fall under the Kansas Opens Record Act' states a legal consequence of AI use that no type covers, so it is UNCOVERED. It informs users, so modality is informs and phase is general.
units.uncovered_note: AI outputs may be public records under the state open-records act; records-law obligations for AI use.

units.passage: Users shall not use Generative AI to generate or enable content that is discriminatory, defamatory, illegal, or in violation of applicable University policy, laws, or regulations. • Users shall not use Generative AI to upload any data that could be used to help create or carry out malware, spam and phishing campaigns or other cyber scams.
units.why: 'Users shall not use Generative AI to upload any data that could be used to help create or carry out malware, spam and phishing campaigns or other cyber scams' bans a cyber-security misuse. P53 covers ethical, bias, labor and environmental concerns, not security attacks, and no other type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Bans uploading data through Generative AI that could help create or carry out malware, spam, phishing campaigns or cyber scams (security misuse).

units.passage: Responses generated from Generative AI shall not: o be used verbatim, o be assumed to be truthful, credible, or accurate, o be used to issue official statements (i.e., policy, legislation, or regulations), o be used to break the University's Principles of Community.
units.why: 'Responses generated from Generative AI shall not ... be used to issue official statements (i.e., policy, legislation, or regulations)' bans one use of AI output in institutional communication. No type covers official statements, and P19 is about work students submit, so UNCOVERED. 'Shall not' gives must-not; it restricts one use within an otherwise permitted frame, so restrict.
units.uncovered_note: Responses generated from Generative AI may not be used to issue official statements such as policy, legislation or regulations.

units.passage: Instances of non-compliance must be presented and reviewed and approved by the Director of Information Security, or equivalent officer. All breaches of information security, actual or suspected, must be reported to and investigated by the Director of Information Security, or equivalent officer. Those who violate security policies, standards, or security procedures are subject to disciplinary action up to and including loss of computer access and appropriate disciplinary actions as determined by the Univers
units.why: 'All breaches of information security, actual or suspected, must be reported to and investigated by the Director of Information Security' sets a duty to report security breaches. units.uncovered_note: Students must first ask for permission, and explain how they plan to use the tool, before using AI on any part of a graded assignment; without permission AI is not allowed. Coder A nearest-type note: Permission is gated on the student asking and explaining the planned use, in a sample statement. Coder B nearest-type note: Asking is mandatory (AI barred without permission) and the student must explain the planned use; P10 is advice to ask when unsure.
